questions.question: What is the relationship between the voltages across individual components in a series circuit and the total voltage of the battery?
options: The individual voltages multiply together to equal the battery voltage.
The individual voltages add up to equal the battery voltage.
The individual voltages are all exactly equal to the battery voltage.
The individual voltages subtract from the battery voltage to equal zero.

questions.question: If three cells, each with a voltage of 1.5 V, are connected in series to make a battery, what is the total voltage of the battery?
Which statement is true about the electric charges in the wires of a circuit when the switch is turned off?
options: Charges are only present in the battery, not in the wires.
Charges are present in all the atoms of the wires.
Charges disappear from the wires completely.
Charges only exist in the light bulbs when off.

questions.question: What happens to the electrons in a circuit immediately after it is turned on?
options: Electrons everywhere in the circuit start moving at the same time.
Electrons start moving from the battery and slowly reach the other end.
Only the electrons inside the light bulb begin to move.
Electrons must first be created by the battery before anything moves.

questions.question: What is the typical speed of individual electrons moving around a circuit?
options: Nearly the speed of light.
Several meters per second.
Just a few millimeters each second.
They remain completely stationary.

questions.question: Why can current not flow through a faulty filament bulb?
options: The glass of the bulb has melted.
The filament is broken, creating a gap.
The bulb has too much resistance.
The gas inside the bulb has escaped.

questions.question: How can you make a series circuit work if one of its components is faulty and blocking the flow?
options: Bypass the faulty component using a wire.
Add a second battery in reverse.
Shake the faulty component to reconnect it.
Increase the thickness of all other wires.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a series circuit?
options: A circuit with multiple branching loops for current to split.
A circuit with one complete loop from one end of a battery to the other end.
A circuit that only functions when a voltmeter is placed in series.
A circuit containing only switches and no power sources.

questions.question: How does an ammeter affect the current in the circuit it is measuring?
options: It significantly reduces the current to protect the circuit.
It increases the current by acting as an extra power source.
It measures the current without affecting the current in the circuit.
It stops the current completely while taking a reading.

questions.question: What is true about the electric current at different points in a series circuit?
options: The current is highest near the positive terminal of the battery.
The current is lowest after passing through a bulb.
The current is the same everywhere in the circuit.
The current constantly fluctuates randomly at different points.

questions.question: If you add an extra bulb to an existing series circuit, what happens to the current?
options: It changes the current everywhere, on both sides of the component.
It only decreases the current after the new bulb.
It only increases the current before the new bulb.
The current remains exactly the same everywhere.

questions.question: How should a voltmeter be connected to measure the voltage across a component?
options: In series, directly inline with the component.
Across the terminals of the component.
Connected only to the positive terminal of the battery.
Wrapped around the plastic insulation of the wire.

questions.question: According to the rules of electrostatic charges, what happens when two objects with the same electric charge are brought near each other?
options: They attract each other.
They repel each other.
They neutralise each other instantly.
They exert no force on each other.

questions.question: What is the name of the negatively charged particles found in atoms?
options: Protons
Neutrons
Electrons
Nuclei

questions.question: Why are metals difficult to charge by rubbing?
options: Metals do not contain any electrons.
Electric charge flows through metals, preventing charge build-up.
Metals repel all forms of static electricity.
Rubbing a metal destroys its atomic structure.
